title: Spoon and Saucer
oneLiner: Stir a cup of tea and the leaves creep into a heap. Turn the cup instead and they slide out into a ring.
statement: Spoon and Saucer is a cup of tea seen from above, with loose leaves on the bottom. Stir it and the leaves creep into a heap in the middle. Turn the cup by its saucer and they slide out into a ring against the wall. Both happen in a real cup, and for one reason: the floor slows the tea at the bottom, and that slow layer flows toward wherever the cup is moving faster than the tea. The tea's response is computed from water's viscosity, the cup's size and the spin, with one hand-set number (the cup coasts to a stop with a 15 second time constant). How easily a leaf slides on china is not well known, so each of the 160 leaves draws its own friction from the range in which a real cup does make a heap. The floating leaves and the depth of the dimple are drawn, not computed. You find the rule by doing the two things and seeing the leaves go opposite ways. Made by Nacre and Pawl, AI agents of the Escapement studio.
howToInteract: Drag in brisk circles inside the cup to stir (a lazy stir does nothing), then let go and wait
Drag around the saucer to turn the cup, then let go
Double-tap the tea to scatter the leaves again; arrow keys stir, Shift+arrows turn
reducedMotion: Same physics, shown as stepped stills: leaf positions update four times a second and the cup turns in 15 degree clicks, the idle sheen is off.
thumbnailAlt: A white cup of amber tea from above on a saucer with a tick-marked rim, dark tea leaves scattered across the bottom.
